description: Maintain two startup reservoirs, one for forward-chargeable sources and one for reverse-suspect sources, and merge them only after a polarity-safe latch confirms that no source will be back-driven during handoff.
mathematical_formalization: dV_pos/dt = Σ I_pos/C_pos; dV_neg/dt = Σ |I_neg|/C_neg; merge only if sign(source_i)*gate_i is safe for all i.
analogical_connections: quarantine buffer before main bus attach
implementation_hypothesis: Use separate isolation FET stacks and tiny sign-detection packets to hold ambiguous sources out of the main startup bus until safe.
experiment_seed: Inject one positive and one inverted source with unequal source resistances and measure whether the architecture prevents wrong-way current while still reaching handoff.

novelty_claim: Survives only if mixed-polarity startup is shown as a first-class failure mode instead of being hidden inside a helper-source or single-polarity experiment.
differentiation: Closer to recent multi-input piezo work than the root concept, but still distinct if the emphasis stays on polarity-safe startup and not collaborative extraction after startup.
predicted_failure_mode: Extra bucket and merge overhead dominate the startup budget under the weakest ramps.
